title: Microsoft Builds Israeli Team to Help Companies Prepare for Quantum Threats
html:
Insider Brief

  • Microsoft is forming a team in Israel to help organizations identify encryption that future quantum computers could break, Calcalist reported.
  • Led by Inbar Badian, the team will develop AI tools to track where organizations use encryption and prioritize weaknesses for repair.
  • Microsoft aims to adopt quantum-resistant cryptography in its critical products and services by 2029.
  • Image: Photo by BoliviaInteligente on Unsplash

Microsoft is forming a team in Israel to help companies identify encryption that future quantum computers could break, Calcalist reported.

Led by Inbar Badian, the group will develop software that uses artificial intelligence to track where organizations use encryption and flag the weaknesses that need attention first. It will use AI agents, software that can carry out tasks on its own, to keep that inventory up to date and help security teams address vulnerabilities, according to the Israeli business and financial newspaper.

The effort is in line with Microsoft’s strategy to accelerate its own shift to post-quantum cryptography, a set of methods designed to withstand quantum computer attacks. The company said in July that it aims to make that transition in critical products and services by 2029.

Finding What Needs to Change

Encryption is built into applications, hardware and cloud services, as well as the connections that carry data between them. That makes it difficult for security teams to see where older protections are still in use, Calcalist reported. When a weakness is discovered, teams first have to determine which systems rely on the affected technology and which handle data sensitive enough to warrant immediate action.

An inventory can also help companies plan the order of an upgrade. A business might be able to update an application it maintains itself, while a change to a cloud service or a piece of network equipment could depend on a supplier. A record of those dependencies gives security teams a way to see where they can act immediately and where they need to coordinate with vendors.

Microsoft has gone through that process itself. The company said its transition began with an inventory across the business to assess risks and decide which to tackle first. It has since added quantum-resistant methods to the underlying security software used by Windows, Azure and Microsoft 365.

Why Companies Are Starting Now

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could break some widely used forms of public-key cryptography, which helps establish secure connections and verify the identity of websites and software publishers. The National Institute of Standards and Technology released its first post-quantum cryptography standards in 2024, giving software makers and organizations a set of replacements to build into their products and systems.

The timing especially matters for information that must remain confidential for years. An attacker could intercept encrypted data today and store it in the hope of reading it once a capable quantum computer exists, a tactic known as harvest now, decrypt later. NIST says integrating new cryptographic standards across products and services can take years, even after the replacements are available.

Badian previously worked in the office of the chief technology officer for Microsoft’s security division, where she helped develop its strategy for quantum readiness, according to Calcalist. The new group will operate within Microsoft’s Israeli research and development center, which was the company’s first outside the U.S. Its largest campus is in Herzliya, and it operates at six locations in Israel.
